module.title: Who should run the government — and who can remove them?
module.subtitle: 5 ways democracies answer this. Each choice reorganizes power differently.

options.label: Parliamentary Confidence
options.mechanism: Prime Minister serves while retaining support of legislature. Removed by vote of no confidence.
options.how_chosen: Selected by legislature / head of state appoints who can command majority
options.how_removed: Vote of no confidence, resignation, election loss
options.checks: Fused - relies on parliament and party discipline

cases.note: Constructive vote of no confidence -> high stability, only 8 chancellors
Fragmented parties + simple confidence -> 40+ governments, instability
Two-party system stabilizes confidence; coalition 2010 tested conventions

options.label: Direct Presidential
options.mechanism: President elected directly by voters for fixed term. Separately legitimized from legislature.
options.how_chosen: Direct popular election (plurality, majority runoff, or electoral college)
options.how_removed: Impeachment, term limit, next election only
options.checks: Strong separation; needs veto-override, judicial review

cases.note: Fixed term + strong checks -> stability but periodic deadlock (e.g. 1860s, 1970s)
Presidential + fragmented multiparty -> coalition presidentialism needed
Single 5-year term designed to prevent entrenchment after authoritarian rule

options.label: Assembly-Appointed
options.mechanism: Legislature elects executive for a term. Executive not continuously dependent on confidence but owes election to assembly.
options.how_chosen: Elected by parliament / assembly, sometimes joint session
options.how_removed: Impeachment / non-reelection, not daily confidence vote
options.accountability: Medium (to assembly, not directly to voters)
options.checks: Assembly supremacy; depends on judicial/councils for balance

cases.note: Federal Council elected by parliament, collegial - extreme stability
Parliament elects President; dominant party dynamics shape accountability
Assembly elects President, long single-party dominance

variants: FR Model: Assembly-Appointed + Judicial Council constraints

options.label: Dual Executive
options.mechanism: Both President (directly elected) and Prime Minister (parliamentary) share executive power with split competencies.
options.how_chosen: President directly elected; PM appointed from parliamentary majority
options.how_removed: PM via confidence; President via impeachment/term end -> cohabitation possible
options.checks: Internal check but rivalry / dual legitimacy risk

cases.note: Semi-presidential works when President has reserve powers; cohabitation 1986, 1993, 1997 managed rivalry
President as arbiter, PM governs - largely cooperative
President + Chancellor dual legitimacy without democratic safeguards -> instability and overreach

options.label: Collegial / Directorial
options.mechanism: Executive power shared equally among council who decide collectively; presidency rotates.
options.how_chosen: Council elected by parliament or directly; chair rotates annually
options.how_removed: Individual or collective non-reelection; collective responsibility
options.checks: Internal mutual veto; resists personalization of power

cases.note: 7-member Federal Council - consensus, stability, low decisiveness
9-member colegiado - attempted consensus but reversed to presidential for decisiveness
Two Captains-Regent, 6-month terms - radical rotation prevents entrenchment

comparison_dimensions.label: Accountability
comparison_dimensions.question: How easily can they be removed when failing?

comparison_dimensions.label: Continuity
comparison_dimensions.question: Will government survive crisis without collapse?

comparison_dimensions.label: Decisiveness
comparison_dimensions.question: Can they act quickly when needed?

comparison_dimensions.label: Coalition Building
comparison_dimensions.question: Does it force compromise or allow solo rule?

interaction_rules.explanation: Both President and legislature claim popular mandates; no majority to govern. Leads to decree use or gridlock.

interaction_rules.then: Flag: Checks Deficit - Executive Overreach Risk
interaction_rules.explanation: Fixed term + popular mandate without strong court or legislature to check power.
President and PM from opposing blocs both claim democratic legitimacy -> competing vetoes.
Easy removal + many small parties = frequent collapses.
